transcript:
Meeting header:
Date/Time: 2027-04-27 15:00 UTC
Duration: 49 minutes
Attendees: Alex Morgan (Redwood AE), Samir Patel (Redwood SE), Karen Liu (Ashford CISO), Diego Ramos (Ashford CTO), Maya Singh (Ashford Legal)

Auto-summary (may be imperfect): Ashford is evaluating options to keep sensitive customer data in EU-only storage, wants assurances around log minimization and redaction for audit, needs BYOK with HSM integration and proof of key residency, and wants a clear map of what data touches Redwood control plane vs customer-controlled components. Agreed next steps include sending security artifacts and scheduling a deeper technical benchmark.

Topics identified: Hosted latency/cost tradeoffs; Dedicated reserved capacity and isolation; Private/VPC with on-prem options; KMS/BYOK and HSM; Log retention windows, redaction & legal hold; Evidence for GDPR deletion; Subprocessor disclosures.

Action items (auto): Alex to send security docs; Samir to draw architecture; Ashford to share dataflow.

Transcript:
[00:00] Alex (AE) - Redwood: Hey, hi everybody, thanks for joining. we got about 45, 50 minutes on the calendar. quick intros?
[00:10] Karen - Ashford (CISO): Karen, I'm the CISO at Ashford, I run security and compliance. we also have Diego our CTO and Maya from legal.
[00:15] Diego - Ashford (CTO): hey all.
[00:17] Samir (SE) - Redwood: Samir, I'm the solutions engineer, I'll take the technical bits.
[00:20] Alex (AE): Awesome. So today's goal is to map residency needs and logging constraints, and then figure out which Redwood hosting mode — hosted, dedicated, or private — fits best. Karen, could you outline the top constraints?
[00:34] Karen: Sure. High level: EU-only storage for a subset of customers, we need KMS keys that we control for that data, minimal logs leaving the region, ability to prove deletion for GDPR right to be forgotten and to respond to audits with chain of custody. also legal hold for litigation might require short-term retention beyond normal windows.
[00:52] Maya - Ashford (Legal): And we'll need assurance that audit logs don't include PII. we have to show redaction or non-capture of sensitive fields.
[01:05] Alex: Understood. quick clarification: when you say "KMS keys you control" do you mean BYOK where your HSM holds the key, or do you mean customer-managed KMS in the cloud?
[01:15] Karen: Ideally BYOK with our HSM -- we run an on-prem HSM that we prefer, but cloud KMS with key import could work if keys never leave our control. ultimately key residency in EU and rotation controls by us.
[01:27] Samir: Ok. Technically we support BYOK via bring-your-own-key integrations, we also have options for customer-managed keys in supported clouds, and for Private deployments you can run an on-prem control plane that never exports keys. small caveat: for Hosted we need to look at which control-plane telemetry is sent out, sometimes meta logs from the control playn — control plane — may leave region unless we pin region for the control plane.
[01:53] Diego: can you detail which logs you mean by meta logs? request/response logs?
[01:58] Samir: yep, there's a couple paths: application payloads (the prompts and responses), operational traces (errors, performance traces), and platform audit logs. for our Hosted product we can enable token-level scrubbing and prefix caching to avoid storing full inputs; however traces and some control-plane metrics may go to our monitoring stack — which can be region-locked for EU customers but there are integrations where certain multi-tenant metadata gets aggregated.
[02:25] Karen: So we need guarantees about no raw prompts emitted to US systems if the tenant is EU. that's non-negotiable.
[02:31] Alex: Point taken. For Dedicated, we can provision EU-only GPU pools and keep all request paths inside EU regions and restrict control-plane endpoints, but the level of isolation differs from Private where the control plane is customer-owned.
[02:46] Maya: Legal question: if Redwood has support engineers access logs for troubleshooting, can we restrict that?
[02:52] Samir: yes. We have role-based access, and in Dedicated and Private we can disable Redwood support access by default and require a jump host or a logged request for any temporary access. We also have audit logs for any support sessions.
[03:07] Maya: good. we will want to see those audit samples.
[03:10] Alex: We'll include sample audit logs in the pack.
[03:13] [03:13] Speaker 1: um, sorry interjection, are you capturing retention windows per-tenant?
[03:18] Samir: yes, retention is configurable per tenant/route. by default Hosted has a 30-day retention for ephemeral telemetry but you can opt into reduced retention, and Dedicated allows custom SLOs. Private gives you full control.
[03:29] Karen: What about legal hold? If we put a legal hold on a customer, will Redwood preserve those records even if retention says delete?
[03:36] Samir: we support legal-hold flags that override deletion; however for Hosted we may still retain encrypted references in control-plane indices for a limited time for operational reasons. we will show how those references contain no PII when redaction is enabled.
[03:51] Diego: what's the proof of deletion you can provide for GDPR? a statement or a tamper-evident log?
[03:58] Alex: We can provide deletion manifests and chain-of-custody statements, plus sanitized audit trails showing deletion operations with timestamps and who initiated them. For Dedicated/Private we can offer more direct proofs because deletion happens in customer-controlled storage buckets.
[04:15] Karen: ok. show me the path for keys in Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private.
[04:20] Samir: Hosted: keys managed by Redwood KMS by default; BYOK via cloud KMS import or external HSM possible with additional contract; some metadata about key IDs may be present in Redwood control-plane, but ciphertext never leaves region if keys are region-bound. Dedicated: you can use a customer-managed cloud KMS instance scoped to your VPC and we can integrate with that; Private: you bring your HSM and we run the control plane inside your environment — keys never leave your network.
[04:44] Karen: how about key escrow / recovery? we need an escrow option if keys are lost.
[04:48] Samir: key escrow is tricky for BYOK — we can offer an optional escrow escrow service where keys are wrapped under a separate escrow HSM that we host inside the EU and only release under strict legal processes. that would be an enterprise add-on.
[05:02] Maya: and what's the legal basis for release — court order, contract?
[05:06] Alex: That's negotiable; typically governed by contract and legal process. we'll flag that as an item for the legal teams to align on.
[05:14] [05:14] Speaker 2: quick question about telemetry: does the K V cache store raw prompts?
[05:18] Samir: The KV cache is an execution artifact, it does not persist raw prompt text to long-term logs by default. But if you enable debugging or detailed traces those artifacts could be written to logs; we recommend disabling debug in prod and enabling scrubbing for Hosted.
[05:34] Diego: If we go Dedicated, are the GPUs completely single-tenant? we still want to confirm no noisy neighbor telemetry.
[05:40] Samir: Dedicated runs in isolated GPU pools provisioned per customer; however the control-plane orchestration can be multi-tenant unless you opt for Private. for the highest assurance you choose Private.
[05:52] Karen: Ok, let's talk about subprocessor list — who are your third parties that may see derivatives or logs?
[05:58] Alex: We'll attach our current subprocessor list; major ones are cloud infra providers in region, monitoring vendors, and a small vector search vendor for embeddings in some configs. we can show which subprocessors are engaged for Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private.
[06:14] Maya: On redaction — we need field-level redaction for PII and the ability to specify regexes or JSON paths to strip before persisting.
[06:22] Samir: We have a data filtering pipeline that supports JSON path redaction and user-supplied regex filters. We'll put some examples in the docs. small caveat: on some older models we recommend you run redaction client-side before sending to inference for maximum assurance.
[06:39] Karen: Will that impact latency?
[06:41] Samir: client-side redaction is negligible; server-side redaction adds a small processing step but is usually sub-100ms per request depending on payload size.
[06:50] Alex: Another point — routing and fallback. If EU region is full, do you want requests to fail or to fall back to a non-EU model?
[06:58] Diego: We need a hard region lock for certain customers. no fallback allowed. for others, failover to other EU regions only.
[07:06] Samir: We can configure routing policies per-tenant: strict-region-lock, region-preferred with failover to other EU regions, or cross-region fallback. we'll show policy examples.
[07:17] Karen: About logs: can you redact before they hit control-plane monitoring?
[07:21] Samir: yes, we have pre-ingest filters; for Hosted we recommend using them. For Dedicated we can also ship forwarding rules to your SIEM inside your VPC. For Private everything stays inside your network.
[07:34] Maya: Regarding legal hold retention beyond usual deletion windows, will we be able to produce a sealed copy of the preserved records for e-discovery?
[07:41] Alex: Yes, we can produce sealed export packages with checksums and access logs. Note that for Hosted there may be extra verification steps.
[07:50] [07:50] Speaker 3: do you support SSO SAML with SCIM provisioning and can we restrict admin roles?
[07:56] Samir: yes we support SAML SSO, SCIM provisioning, and granular RBAC. In Dedicated/Private you can enforce stricter policies and remove Redwood admins from default roles.
[08:06] Karen: Any compliance reports for healthcare? HIPAA?
[08:09] Alex: We have HIPAA controls and execute BAAs for Private and Dedicated customers. Hosted requires a review, and we can sign a BAA for covered use cases but may require additional controls. we'll include our HIPAA mapping.
[08:23] Diego: Can you demonstrate how logs are redacted in practice? maybe a short recording or sample?
[08:28] Samir: We'll include sanitized samples and a short demo clip showing pre-ingest redaction.
[08:34] Maya: On SSO auditability, we need login events exported to our SIEM and retention for seven years for compliance — does Redwood allow exporting audit logs to customer SIEM?
[08:44] Samir: yes, we have log forwarders and can push to common destinations (Splunk, SumoLogic, customers' cloud logging) with TLS and signed delivery.
[08:53] Alex: Quick note on billing and data location: billing metadata sometimes crosses borders for payment processing; we can separate billing metadata from payload metadata in many cases. we'll call that out.
[09:04] Karen: Good to know. What about pentest evidence and recent vulnerability timelines?
[09:09] Alex: We'll attach the most recent penetration test summary and CVE remediation timeline.
[09:15] [09:15] Speaker 1: how do you handle backup snapshots? Are they encrypted and region-located?
[09:21] Samir: Backups are encrypted with KMS keys and stored in region by default; snapshot copies to other regions require explicit config and business justification.
[09:31] Diego: If we opt for Private, what's the ops overhead? we can't take on too much.
[09:36] Samir: There's more operational overhead for Private — you run the control plane or host it, and you manage HSMs and backups; we provide an ops playbook, automation templates and a managed-support option where Redwood handles day-to-day under an SLA.
[09:53] Karen: can you outline the support model for emergency extracts / legal requests?
[09:57] Alex: We have a documented process: formal support request with approval chain, time-bound temporary access, audit logs of the session, and an after-action report. We'll include the runbook.
[10:08] Maya: we will need the contract language for that.
[10:11] Alex: noted.
[10:13] [10:13] Speaker 2: small thing — do we get the subprocessor termination notice if you change vendors?
[10:18] Alex: Yes, we send notice and we maintain a published subprocessor page and notify customers per contract terms.
[10:25] Diego: We're interested in pilot scope. what would you suggest?
[10:29] Samir: A two-week pilot scoped to a non-production tenant: we route traffic through an EU-only Dedicated pool, enable pre-ingest redaction, integrate with your KMS (BYOK), and run a set of benchmark prompts and retention/delete tests. We'll capture latency, throughput, and proof-of-deletion runs.
[10:48] Karen: Cost?
[10:49] Alex: We'll send a pilot estimate; Dedicated pilot pricing is usually a short-term reserved instance plus professional services.
[10:56] Maya: Legal will need a pilot agreement and data processing addendum.
[11:00] Alex: we'll draft that.
[11:02] [11:02] Speaker 3: any thoughts on encryption-in-transit cert management? do we need to manage certs?
[11:07] Samir: TLS endpoints are managed by Redwood by default; for Private/Dedicated we can use your certs via ACM or on-prem cert management.
[11:16] Diego: latency targets for customer-facing features — we'll need <100ms p95 for short prompts. can you meet that with redaction on?
[11:24] Samir: yes, with Dedicated EU pools and small redaction overhead we generally meet sub-100ms for typical payload sizes, we'll include benchmark numbers.
[11:33] Karen: a few edge items: data subject access requests — will Redwood assist in searching past prompts to find PII?
[11:40] Samir: We provide tooling that can search sanitized indices and we can run forensics on export packages. For Hosted, access requires coordination; for Private you own the indices so it is straightforward.
[11:53] Alex: All right, I want to confirm the hard requirements we've heard: (1) EU-only residency for a subset of tenants with strict region lock; (2) BYOK with HSM residency in EU; (3) pre-ingest redaction and field-level filters; (4) legal-hold overrides; (5) auditable deletion proofs. Anything else?
[12:16] Karen: also subprocessor transparency and ability to restrict forwarding to our SIEM.
[12:21] Maya: and the pilot must include deletion proof runs.
[12:24] Alex: Great. We'll deliver items and schedule the technical deep dive.
[12:28] Samir: I'll take lead on architecture and demo.
[12:31] Diego: we'll assign two infra engineers to the deep dive.
[12:34] Alex: any other quick questions before we wrap?
[12:37] Karen: one last — are there any hidden logs created by autoscaling components we should be aware of?
[12:43] Samir: autoscaler logs exist but you can opt them out of long-term storage; by default they're short-lived and anonymized. We'll list them out.
[12:53] Maya: thanks, that helps.
[12:55] Alex: next steps recap: Alex will send security pack by 5/1; Samir will send architecture and sample redaction configs by 5/5; Ashford will share dataflow and retention policy by 5/4; schedule technical deep dive week of 5/10.
[13:19] Karen: good. thanks everyone.
[13:21] Diego: thanks.
[13:22] Samir: thanks all.
[13:25] Alex: bye.

Note: transcription includes occasional speaker mislabels and small recognition errors (e.g., "control playn" instead of control plane, "K V cache"). Full detail artifacts to be provided in follow-ups as attachments.
